claims.content: The user has launched the PeaZip application.
The user is viewing a file manager interface within PeaZip that displays files or folders located on a storage unit supported by the operating system.
The user has selected one or more specific files or folders intended for secure deletion from the displayed list.
The user initiates the secure deletion function by selecting 'Secure delete' from the 'File Tools' menu or using the associated keyboard shortcut (Shift+Del).
PeaZip performs multiple successive passes of random data writing over the storage area occupied by the selected files or folders to ensure data recovery is not possible.
Upon completion of the overwrite process, PeaZip removes the file entries from the file system, effectively deleting them.

If the selected file or folder is located on a read-only storage medium (e.g., CD-ROM) or a network drive where write access is restricted, PeaZip cannot perform the overwrite passes required for secure deletion. The system displays an error message indicating insufficient permissions or read-only status and aborts the operation.

If the user attempts to securely delete a file that is currently open or locked by another process or the operating system, PeaZip fails to gain exclusive access to the file handle. The system notifies the user that the file is in use and cancels the secure deletion procedure.

If the secure deletion process is interrupted by a system crash, power failure, or forced termination of the application during the multiple overwrite passes, the file data may be partially overwritten but not fully erased according to the security standard. The file entry may remain in the file system in a corrupted state, requiring manual cleanup by the user.
The selected files and folders are permanently removed from the file system.
The data previously occupying the storage space of the deleted items has been overwritten with random data, rendering it unrecoverable by standard data recovery tools.
The file manager interface is updated to reflect the absence of the securely deleted items.
